deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is an anatomical-mechanical description of the middle-ear ossicles, written as the descriptive groundwork for Riemann's fragment on the mechanics of the ear. Henle published a version of that fragment posthumously in 1866/67 as "Mechanik des Ohres" (Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin). Content in order:

(1) Model of the ossicular chain. It is treated as two rigid parts:
- a compound body made of the malleus (Hammer) and incus (Ambos), which rotates about a fixed axis;
- the stapes (Steigbügel), which articulates with that body and presses on the oval window (fenestra vestibuli, 'Fenster des Vorhofs').

(2) The rotation axis is fixed at its two ends:
- Posterior end: the short process of the incus, held by the incudal ligament ('Ambos-Paukenband') to the posterior wall of the tympanic cavity.
- Anterior end: the long (anterior, Folian) process of the malleus. Surrounded by ligamentous tissue, it projects into a fissure between the anterior-superior end of the tympanic ring and the squama (the petrotympanic/Glaserian fissure). It rests against a process of that ring (a tympanic spine; the rest of this parenthesis is illegible).

In modern terms this is the 'axis ligament' picture of the malleus–incus block: one rigid body with one rotational degree of freedom about the line joining the anterior mallear ligament and the posterior incudal ligament.

(3) Reference frame. Positions are described using Henle's convention: imagine the tympanic cavity rotated so that the rotation axis is horizontal and the stapes stands vertical. In that frame the tympanic membrane is not exactly parallel to the axis; its posterior part is turned slightly laterally.

The cancelled lines show Riemann reworking exactly this last statement about the membrane's orientation relative to the axis. Nothing is derived; there is no formula to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical or anatomical errors identifiable. The description matches standard anatomy: the incus short process is held by the posterior incudal ligament, and the malleus anterior process sits in the petrotympanic fissure. The heavily cancelled final lines are drafts, not errors.

results.what: Malleus and incus treated as one rigid body rotating about a fixed axis through the anterior process of the malleus and the short process of the incus, with the stapes as a separate articulated piece pressing on the oval window
results.modern_name: Axis-ligament (fixed-axis rotation) model of the ossicular chain
results.usually_credited_to: Helmholtz, 'Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen und des Trommelfells' (1868); earlier anatomical descriptions by Henle and others

results.what: Orientation convention: rotate the tympanic cavity so the axis is horizontal and the stapes vertical; the tympanic membrane is then slightly turned laterally at its posterior part relative to the axis
results.modern_name: Anatomical reference-frame convention for the middle ear

deep.surprise_reason: Purely descriptive anatomy that forms part of Riemann's known posthumous fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres', published by Henle. It contains no mathematics and nothing beyond what that published fragment and contemporary anatomy already record.
transcription_corrections: 'auf das Fenster des Vorhofs drückenden' is confirmed: the oval window, fenestra vestibuli.
The rotation axis is called 'Umdrehungsaxe'; the clause reads 'Das eine Ende der Umdrehungsaxe, der kurze Fortsatz des Ambos'.

The anterior end is 'der lange Fortsatz des Hammers' (processus anterior/Folianus). It lies 'in eine Spalte zwischen dem vordern obern Ende des Trommelfellringes und der Schuppe'; 'und der Schuppe' is an interlinear insertion.
Line 'Die Bestimmung der Lage ...': 'relativen' is struck. In 'dass die Umdrehungsaxe horizontal [hinten nach vorn struck] geht', 'geht' is inserted above the line.

The final cancelled block is most plausibly: 'Das Trommelfell steht dabei nicht genau parallel zur Umdrehungsaxe ..., sondern ist mit seinem hintern Theile ein wenig lateralwärts gedreht.' Only 'hintern Theils ein wenig lateralwärts gedreht' is uncancelled.
The parenthesis after 'Fortsatz dieses Ringes' is largely illegible. 'Spina' (spina tympanica) is plausible; 'ist also kaum ... des Knöchelchens' is uncertain.
